newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-April 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Beijing has instructed the Chinese media to help change the view of people in the West that socialism was against human rights.
-- Bank of East Asia chairman David Li said he was worried that foreign funds might pull out of Hong Kong after the handover, which would cause stock market volatility.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- The office of chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa announced that HK$107.8 million (US$14 million) would be required to set up the territory's post-handover government.

-- Tung's office would issue proposals for revisions of two human rights ordinances for consultation today, in which the concept of national security would be introduced for the first time in Hong Kong.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese Vice-Premier and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, discussing China-Taiwan relations on a tour of Fujian province, stressed that the interests of Taiwanese investors would be protected on the mainland.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Bankers said Hong Kong banks might be able to lend more to China and other non-OECD countries in the event of a change to the Bank for International Settlements' risk-asset weighting standards on such lending.

--The Hong Kong Futures Exchange was to train a group of hand-picked Hong Kong Chinese candidates from which it would choose a chief executive for the exchange in 2001, the year after newly-appointed chief Robert Gilmore's contract expires.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The number of Hong Kong people seeking permits to visit Taiwan has risen sharply as many see the island as an alternative in the face of uncertainties after the handover.
